spans.text: Hold on!
A familiar figure flits past. Shadowless dashes out of the reception room in pursuit, but the figure is nowhere to be seen.
She stands at the intersection and glares sullenly at the empty hallways.
Sh-Shadow!
You gave me such a scare... What's the matter with you? Why did you run off all of a sudden?
What if we made a bad impression on Mrs. Gray?!
The assistant comes running after Shadowless and admonishes her while still out of breath.
Shadowless finally gives up. She turns back and shakes her head at her assistant.
Sorry, I thought I saw someone I knew...
Did Mrs. Gray say anything?
Well, no...
Really? That woman sure is a crafty one.
Shadow!
The assistant's eyes widen in alarm.
That's Mrs. Gray you're talking about! How could you say that?
Eli, if you truly want to become a good reporter, you must learn to see through these celebrities' facades for whom they really are.
But Mrs. Gray feels genuinely like a good person...
Besides, we really do need cheaper drugs desperately.
They finally developed one. Isn't this fantastic news for the people?
Personal morals are irrelevant to people like her.
I'll refrain from commenting on Mrs. Gray's position, but she is very smart and knows exactly what we reporters want to hear—I'll give her that.
She always says just the right thing to win people over.
She didn't get to where she is today with just her pretty face.
Shadowless shoves her hands into the pockets of her trench coat and looks in the direction of the reception room with a piercing gaze that seems to see through all deception.
Idunn could indeed be an effective cure... But this cake will be gobbled up long before the people who need it most can even get to it.
Remember, Eli—our job as the media is to uncover and piece together the truth.
The nature of our work requires us to be critical of everything we see.
At the very least, we must give the full picture so that the public can have all the facts, and not just things that these people want them to know.
...This is way too dark.
Your way of looking at things, I mean.
It's reality, Eli.
These corporations and the government are all birds of a feather.
Don't be fooled by their glamorous appearance. In the end, the only ones we can trust are ourselves.
Shadowless watches as her other colleagues leave the reception room with all their packed equipment.
Let's head back.
Okay...
The group make for the main exit with Shadowless trailing behind. She stops and looks back at the hallway behind her.
Shadow?
Coming.
After the press corps has left, Light strolls out from a corner that Shadowless' gaze has swept over.
...Her sixth sense is sharp as ever.
Click.
Light, where are you?
We're done over here.
Right. I'll be right there.
Light turns off his comms and strokes his chin.
...She didn't see me, I hope.
With a faint sense of unease, he once again retreats into the blind spot of the CCTV system.
